qt: to the Council Christine Anderson (ESN), Marieke Ehlers (PfE), Tomasz Froelich (ESN), Milan Uhrík (ESN), Markus Buchheit (ESN), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Volker Schnurrbusch (ESN), Mary Khan (ESN) Subject:

In its reply1 of 26 October 2026 to parliamentary question E-004707/20252, the Council stated that inclusion on the EU terrorist list requires a decision by a competent authority of a Member State or third country. It left unanswered whether Antifa Ost (‘Hammerbande’) meets these requirements or whether a listing procedure is under way. Hungary designated Antifa Ost as a terrorist organisation in September 2025 and maintained this designation in 20263. The United States designated the group as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist on 13 November 2025 and as a Foreign Terrorist Organization on 20 November 20254. Meanwhile, the ongoing criminal trial in Dresden has attracted renewed attention following the death of a defendant after a suicide attempt in October 20265. The Council is asked: 1.
Is it currently examining the inclusion of Antifa Ost on the EU terrorist list on the basis of the Hungarian or US decisions, and when can a decision be expected?
Do these decisions satisfy the requirements of Article 1(4) of Common Position 2001/931/CFSP6, and what additional conditions, if any, must be met?
What specific legal or factual obstacles currently prevent the inclusion of Antifa Ost on the EU terrorist list?
